query: Which small-cluster inference methods and exact cluster-count cutoffs work best for <30, 30–50, and >50 clusters with serial correlation?

response.query: Which small-cluster inference methods and exact cluster-count cutoffs work best for <30, 30–50, and >50 clusters with serial correlation?
response.answer: For small clusters, hierarchical clustering works best; for larger clusters, k-means is effective; exact cutoffs depend on dataset specifics but often range from 10 to 50 for optimal results.

results.title: Reinforcement Learning and Decision Making
results.content: I watched the lectures by David Silver and those prepared me for all projects and quizzes but not for the final (that’s why the B). I was in sync with the learnings and lectures for the first month or so, but with so many different papers and algorithms and mainly, the projects, it all went to he'll soon after xD. The six homeworks are auto-graded in Gradescope and cover the material from the lectures/readings and help give a good foundation for thinking about the projects. The projects are interesting in that you are *not* graded on your implementation at all, but rather on your interpretation of your results, and the exam is a multiple choice exam that covers all of the material in the course. The lectures (which are hours per week) are completely disjoint from the projects, but certainly not the final. Likewise the required lectures are not useful for the projects beyond week 2-3; most students recommend watching a different set of lectures (David Silver).
